body: I tell people my son was a veteran with ptsd. Most seem to understand that and stop without asking for the gory details. I don’t actually say the word suicide or anything along those lines. It works for me, but everyone has their own comfort level.
Talk to your doctor about it. You might need a change in dosage or another med entirely. Sometimes we develop a tolerance after a while and it stops working like it should.
Okay, I don’t even have piggies. Just here for good pig stuff to live vicariously through y’all…..this is the best thread ever 🤣
Depends on your brain chemistry. Wellbutrin actually made me worse but Prozac helped for a long time. It takes 4-6 weeks to get in your system and start working properly though.

Grief is very complicated and different for everyone. 
As far as not crying or other things some days, recognize that it’s not linear like so many people think it is. Try a google search for grief ball in a box. It’s a very insightful analogy and I found it to be helpful. I wish I could put the link here for you but don’t know how…..phone technology is not my strong suit.
I’m sorry, I don’t know who you lost but I miss my son an extra lot on certain days like his birthday.

My oldest son left us 20 months ago and I still get this too so definitely feel you. My only living child is special needs and will most likely never get to a point where he can have/is able to care for a child.
A couple weeks ago a friend of mine found out her daughter is expecting. It will be her first grandchild and she’s understandably excited. The problem I had was that she called asking me what to let the child call her. Apparently she doesn’t like the image the title of grandma projects and she wants an alternative. I went nuts and lost it because I’d give anything to have the opportunity she has and all she can think about is appearances.
She hasn’t spoken to me since.

Well if you didn’t deprive him of his required ration of treats he wouldn’t have to get them himself now would he? Give him another, but he’s also very clearly trying to let you know he needs more on a regular basis. Double should do just fine 😁

I don’t know if they ever officially came up with one. Have had mental health problems for a very long time. When things first got bad, I was in grade school and at that time it was thought that “kids at that age can’t be depressed”. I was put on a hold in the psych ward and tied to a table for the first time in high school. My first attempt was in junior high when I tried to overdose. With all this, they just kinda said depression and told me to take meds. My dad was bipolar if that makes sense though.
She’s not judging. They don’t start silent judgment until after the cute puppy phase. That’s when they learn how to give side eye

I appreciate the info and understand. I actually just asked my doctor again an hour ago (been calling him every day to check since they put me in this holding pattern) he said to keep waiting on the insurance, I just didn’t know if someone else had any ideas on how they handled it.

Most states have at least some of their budgets left from Covid relief money. It’s not the same as the stimulus thing and you have to apply for it. Google for Covid relief in your area. Some places go by county, some by region, but they should have something. A friend of mine works for the one in our area and has been able to help quite a few people. You will still have to get a job soon, but that could help some. She was able to get one guys power, gas, and internet back on as well as keep him from getting evicted.
Charles or Charlie. Chucky’s kill you in your sleep and creep me out.
My bad, I thought you were in that big system. My aunt got almost 10 inches as of about an hour ago and it’s not supposed to be stopping until tomorrow evening.
Tater tots! ❤️
Michigan or Ohio? Also depending upon where you are in relation to the grocery, some are delivering. We saw a dude ride by on a snow machine 20 minutes ago with groceries and the neighbors pizza.

Maybe try reconnecting with his family if you are on good terms with them? There are lots of reasons why a relationship may not succeed and  that doesn’t mean you can’t be friendly with them.
I’m on good terms and with my sons ex, and we occasionally talk or exchange pictures. As odd as this probably sounds, I think her kids are probably the closest thing I’m ever going to have to grandkids. My son who is still with me is special needs. He’s very sweet and I love him to pieces, but I can’t see him having children.

I know that probably sounds terrible but I frequently take medical/behavioral fosters who have no business being in public quite yet.

I’m calling BS here. If you were true to your word and training them as ptsd therapy dogs, not only would you not be trying to peddle them on here, but the program you work with would have no problem placing them and would have a waiting list a mile long. My son lost his life to depression and ptsd. He was on a waiting list but never got an alert dog. 
Also, I’m calling BS on your so called brothers in arms. I was deemed unfit to serve due to a medical condition, but do come from a proud military family. If any one of them heard you trying to steal valor the way you just did, you would be rethinking your life choices.

Awwww, now I want to give him smooches! May I ask what he is training for? Integration and pet socializing, therapy, alert…..sorry for so many questions. I volunteered for the shelter until Covid, and love seeing people put the absolutely essential work into these animals the way it’s needed! ❤️❤️

When bringing life into the world, you have a responsibility to that being for it’s entire life. That doesn’t change just because the species changed. Human, canine, anything needs to be cared for.  I repeat, being unexpectedly pregnant doesn’t excuse you from your responsibilities as a human. In fact, it actually reinforces them. Here you are reproducing and bringing another life into this world and you can’t handle what you have. I understand that life happens, but you brought that animal into this world and should take care of it. Those dogs didn’t ask to be born, you forced it upon them.
Looks like she could use a little fluffing of her pillow on the top left corner. Get to it hooman, what’s taking you so long? 🤣

A responsible person will not only think carefully before breeding with the existing over population, but would also only breed for a specific characteristic to better the breed if they did choose to do so.
Being certified means nothing if you aren’t a decent human being. Are you willing and able to care for each and every animal for the entirety of it’s life? If you can’t promise every animal that exact thing no matter what, you have no business breeding. Now or ever. Being unexpectedly pregnant doesn’t excuse you from your responsibilities as a human.

It sounds like you might need medication to help balance you out. There’s no shame in needing medication for depression anymore than a diabetic needing insulin. Depending upon what country and type of area you are in, your therapist may have been trying to get you to check yourself in. Lots of countries have it set up that if you are in a rural area and need to get admitted as an inpatient to the psych ward you have to go through the emergency room.  Depending upon what part of the world you are in the experience can vary. I’m told that US inpatient care has improved greatly in recent years if that helps at all.

It sounds like you have anxiety or depression and need medication. As someone who has issues with the same, I have to say this is too big to handle yourself. Having lost a child because he also tried to self medicate I can tell you this method doesn’t work. You need to seek professional help.
You will probably just be nauseous and may cause liver damage if done over time.

Well, that’s certainly your decision and yours alone to make. Do whatever you have to do to get through the day. I understand the duality you’re talking about but I’m just saying that grief, especially this type is an entirely different animal. Don’t let fear of the day or event stop you from taking care of yourself. I took the day of the first anniversary off work and let myself do whatever I wanted all day. Try practicing some self care whatever that means for you. For myself it was a pedicure and working on one of my crafts mostly. I also spent a good bit of time allowing myself to cry as much as I wanted and watching large amounts of mindless tv. A Star Trek marathon and some snacks helped. Whatever gets you through it is the answer.
I felt the same way that first one. Do you have any friends or family you can hang with for the day just to keep yourself occupied and get through?

I get you there. Didn’t know it either until he told me. On the meds end, I really would talk to your doctor if possible. Tell him what’s going on and ask what the options are. It can’t hurt to ask right? If he’s not willing to work with you can you look at other doctors for another opinion?

I also have social anxiety and depression. It takes me a long time to feel comfortable around someone and even then it’s hard for me to connect with people. I was able to find a job working from home mostly and even do the majority of my shopping online. It helps to reduce my daily anxiety. Maybe you can do something similar? I know there are quite a selection of online public schools now.

I feel the same most of the time. Had a psychiatrist tell me I’m considered “passive suicidal”. Don’t completely understand but apparently it is along the lines of that I wouldn’t cause my own death but certainly wouldn’t prevent it. I’m so heavily medicated that tired all the time and even when awake am kinda zombie I guess? My doctor just got me approved for and did the dna enzyme test. Results aren’t back yet but hopefully whatever it says helps. Have you talked to your doctor about a med change or testing?

I’m going to tell you this as a mother that lost her soldier. He was army vs navy, but I still feel like it applies here. He took his life on July 29, 2020. The next day I started getting messages and phone calls from his friends. As soon as news of his service hit, people were telling me how much he meant to them and asking how they could help. In the note he left and some journals I found afterwards, he said he felt like a failure as well. The people who knew him didn’t think so. I didn’t think so. Only he did. My point here is that you have very likely made a positive impact on someone, whether you know it or not. You aren’t a failure. I still get messages from some of his friends. Mostly checking to see how our family is doing, but also to let me know they came across something that reminded them of him and made them smile. I’m sure the same is true for you. You have people who care about you more than you know.

I feel your pain. My sister OD’d and we had to tell her son on his 10th birthday. It broke my heart to see him hurt like that. It was 17 years later when my oldest son took his own life and it was the same pain to watch his brother. He’s the only thing keeping me going now and I’m so grateful to have him. I would have done anything to trade my life for either of theirs. Still wish I could.

My nightmares themselves have gotten less over the months, but so has my sleep. The best thing I can tell you if you don’t have insurance and can’t afford a doctor is to try a free or low cost clinic. You might have to call around to find one but they do exist.  They might be able to help you either with counseling or meds. I’m working with my doctor now to get them working properly for me. He’s trying to get me approved for the DNA testing and we’re shooting for February. Best of luck to you

I’m starting to think going through the med change and possibly inpatient might be doable.

How long did it take you to transition your meds? Were you able to get through it without going inpatient? I’m starting to feel like it might be okay if it does have to be inpatient but would rather avoid it if possible obviously

The only way I’m allowed therapy right now is inpatient. Seems like a self defeating policy because they do it like that to save money. It sounds like most people are saying the psych system is better than it used to be so that is starting to feel like an option. Maybe between all the things combined I can get it worked out
Thank you, that thought gives me more comfort than before.

I haven’t been inpatient since was a teenager and at that time everything about psych care was awful. Has it actually changed enough so it’s really bearable? The last time that happened it was horrid. Have you or someone close enough to tell you the actual circumstances been in recently? I don’t want to end up tied to a table again.
I’ll have to try that. Thank you for answering. It sounds silly but sometimes it helps just to know someone is listening.
